notes:
IMPORTANT: "Countryman Type 85" is not a lavalier microphone. In Countryman's real catalog, Type 85 (SKU DT85) is the Type 85 FET Direct (DI) Box — a 1-channel active instrument direct box that converts a high-impedance instrument/pickup signal to a balanced mic-level signal. Countryman's actual lavalier microphones use different model names (B3, B6, E6, EMW, Isomax) — no lavalier called "Type 85" exists. Returning the real DT85 product since that is the exact name requested.

Ports: front panel has two 1/4" (6.35mm) TS jacks labeled "INST." (instrument input) and "AMP." (parallel unity-gain thru-output feeding the player's stage amp), confirmed from Countryman's own product photography. The balanced output is XLR-type per Countryman's own product copy ("connects...to a balanced microphone (XLR type) input"), corroborated by B&H's spec sheet and Sweetwater/Full Compass listings; its exact printed panel label was not independently visually confirmed (likely unlabeled or "OUTPUT" on the rear end-cap, standard for this DI form factor).

Power: no external DC power port. Runs on 48V phantom power (0.4 mA, drawn through the XLR output pins) or an internal 9V battery (~400 hrs on alkaline) — since there's no external power connector, no power port is listed.

Not included as a port: a front-panel slide switch selects PICKUP vs SPEAKER input mode (changes gain -10dB/-46dB and input impedance 10MΩ/10kΩ) — this is a mode switch, not a physical I/O connector.

A 2-channel sibling product, "Type 85S Direct Box," also exists in Countryman's current lineup.

No bandwidth-graded connector types are present (pure analog audio: TS + XLR3), so no "grade" fields apply.
